applied.change: agentic-stack instruction 7 now states that the root skill's own composes_with is empty by design and that the validator exempts the root from the used_by symmetry check, so 'Builds on: -' reads as exempt rather than unused; composes_with itself was left untouched because the manifest governs links.

Narrowed build-adapter-pair best practice from a claim about de facto standards in general to what F-a4-08 shows: one widely adopted route branches on three provider names and refuses a fourth, so check that the route both adapters depend on admits both.

Added contract.shapes to build-adapter-pair (origin proposed): a JSON Schema 2020-12 array shape for differs_in_execution_model with an enum of the seven execution-model axes, today_value, second_value and an optional measured flag; the invariant and instructions 3 and 4 now point at it instead of describing the field in prose three times.

build-skill-authoring step 11 now says seven existing layers and names root alongside core, cap, xc, seam, compose and build, noting root is reserved for the root contract alone and that a new prefix would be the eighth.

Moved the 145-line evidence-record JSON Schema into references/evidence-record-shape.md, left a ~20-line summary shape in contract.shapes naming that file, and merged the 12-row instructions table down to 10 rows (run identity merged; upgrade and contradiction merged into one append-only correction step; verify-then-cite merged), with a new proposed instruction saying when to open the reference. Rendered SKILL.md fell from 331 to 185 lines.

Stopped restating F-a7-03 in three places: agentic-stack keeps the canonical green-gate row, while build-adapter-pair and build-skill-authoring now carry proposed rows that name the root contract and add only their own consequence, and build-evidence-record's duplicate best-practice row was deleted (its instruction on scoping the measured label is its single use).

Tightened build-evidence-record's first trigger clause from 'about to write down a result' to 'about to record a definition-of-done outcome or an entry in the evidence store', so the description no longer fires on every written statement.

brief_changes: Replaced the size guidance with checked budgets: 6 to 10 instructions, 3 to 10 invariants, 3 to 8 best practices, roughly 3 to 10 rows per table, and an explicit threshold that a schema over about 25 rendered lines is long material whose full form belongs in references/ with a summary shape in contract.shapes.

Added a 'Defects found in ceremony 1' section with six numbered rules: seven layers with root reserved for agentic-stack; compose by name rather than restating a builds_on neighbour's fact; every machine-readable field named in prose needs a contract.shapes entry; origin=sourced covers scope as well as wording, so do not widen a fact into a claim about a class; write description triggers that fire on the skill's actual scope; and do not 'fix' the root skill's deliberately empty composes_with.

Added a 'What worked in wave 1' section (verbatim quotes copied from kb.py show, honest claimed-versus-measured definitions of done, one canonical statement of a shared design rule) so the next authors keep those habits.
Moved the reply instruction to the end of the brief so the new material reads before it.
lessons_for_next_section: Before a skill claims to enumerate anything in this repo (layers, rules, components), read the enum in schemas/skill.schema.json or the dict in tools/validate_skills.py and count from it.
A fact stated by a skill under builds_on is cited by name plus kb id, never re-worded; each skill adds only the consequence that is new in its own context.
Any field an instruction calls machine-readable gets a contract.shapes JSON Schema in the same skill, or the next author has only prose to code against.
origin=sourced must match the scope of the record, not just contain a verbatim quote; the validator checks the quote, so over-generalization is the reviewer's job to catch and the author's to avoid.
Write the schema and the worked examples straight into references/<file>.md with a proposed instruction naming when to open it, instead of inlining them and trimming later.
Description trigger clauses should name an artifact or a moment; a clause broad enough to fire on any sentence in the repo is a defect, not thorough coverage.
